The value behind the title

Make the operational side feel lighter.

I work alongside business owners, CEOs and executive leaders to turn priorities into coordinated action. I manage people and day-to-day operations, improve the systems behind the work, and build practical automations that remove repeat handling. I stay hands-on: the goal is not simply to finish tasks, but to give leaders clearer visibility, stronger follow-through and more room to focus on decisions and growth.

No jargon requiredWhat the work means in everyday business terms
CRMA shared system for customer or client details, current status, history, and the next action.
WorkflowThe sequence a piece of work follows—from the first input to the finished result.
AutomationSoftware handles consistent, repeatable steps so people can focus on checking quality and making decisions.
SOPA written, step-by-step guide that helps a team complete recurring work in a consistent way.

Before / after · 01

Repetitive document preparation: about 2 minutes instead of 10–20

A recurring business document took 10–20 minutes to prepare each time. I built a Google Docs + Google Sheets automation to standardize information, prepare the document consistently and keep human review in the process.

10–20 minutes → about 2 minutes per item
Google DocsGoogle SheetsGoogle Apps Script
Reported department-wide adoption

Fewer repeated steps · 02

Connect forms, record updates and follow-ups

The process depended on several separate forms, manual record updates and follow-up steps. I consolidated the forms into one coordinated pipeline: information is collected once, the client record and pipeline stage are updated, and the next follow-up is triggered through the connected system. A pipeline is simply the shared view of where each request or client file stands and what needs to happen next.

About 20 minutes → about 5 minutes end-to-end
Google WorkspaceLawmaticsSlack
Clearer status and follow-up
▤
Consistency by design · 03

File Renamer: standardize file names automatically

When each file is named by hand, formats can drift and files become harder to find. I built a File Renamer using Google Apps Script and Google Workspace. It reads permitted file details, applies a consistent naming rule and generates a standard file name—so people do not have to rename every file manually. I describe the result as improved consistency and fewer manual steps, not an unmeasured time-saving percentage.

One repeatable naming rule · fewer manual naming steps
Google SheetsGoogle Apps ScriptGoogle Drive
No unsupported time-saved claim
